plain: A mid-century American inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have found a way to move things with high-voltage electricity, a way to "transcend" chemical combustion, meaning engines that burn fuel. Michels raises it on several episodes, placing the work in the 1950s, and on one he goes further, saying he has "independently uncovered an absurd amount of information" that leads him to believe Brown "essentially discovered anti-gravity." If true, a way to fly without rockets or jets has been known for decades.
